title: One playbook walk keeps every parsed role spec tree in memory, about 85x its raw bytes, roughly 1.4 GB live per sync
description: The walk of one playbook limits the raw bytes it reads to 16 MiB (maxWalkBytes), 512 KiB per file. It keeps every parsed role argument-spec document (the yaml.Node tree and its yamlFile) referenced from w.specs and w.sources until the walk ends. It does this even when the spec cannot be used, for example a sequence instead of a mapping, so the role is reported as unreadable. A dense YAML flow list keeps about 84.5 bytes of heap per raw byte. One playbook that lists 31 roles, each with a 512 KiB meta/argument_specs.yml, therefore holds about 1.37 GB of live heap. With the default GOGC=100 the peak heap can reach about twice that. The walk ends normally: no walk cap trips, and the playbook is not even marked failed. Anyone who can push to a repository an org has configured can trigger this. The worker parses the clone in-process on every sync, and syncs can be webhook-triggered, so no human runs a job first. The memory is freed when the walk ends, so the effect is a transient peak once per sync. Whether that peak kills the worker, or other processes on a shared host (the bundled compose runs the worker next to the manager and Postgres with no memory limits), depends on the deployment. Measured in the sandbox at commit 52f27625: the retained heap grows linearly at 84.5x raw bytes. It was 44.3 MB for 1 role, 354 MB for 8, 709 MB for 16 and 1.06 GB for 24 (12 MiB raw). The playbook was not failed, and the heap dropped back to about 160 KB after the walk (agents/v06-varsource/artifacts/evidence.txt). Imported playbook files also stay referenced through w.sources and their yamlFile entry caches. The fix should therefore bound everything a walk keeps parsed, not only the role specs.
claimed_root_cause: walk.spec (internal/varsource/roles.go:297-326) parses each spec file once per walk and stores the document root and its yamlFile in w.specs (line 324) and w.sources (line 322) for the rest of the walk. This is so that several entry points (tasks_from) of one file share one parse. The walk's limits (maxWalkBytes and the per-file MaxFileBytes on raw bytes, maxWalkSteps on nodes visited, maxWalkReadBytes on scalar bytes read) charge raw input and visits. None of them charges the nodes a parse creates and keeps. A large node that is never visited costs no steps, so a 16 MiB walk can keep about 85x that in yaml.Node trees.

trace.description: During every repository sync (webhook-triggered too), the worker parses the cloned repository content in-process through varsource.ParseRepoInstalled. That content is lower trust than the org admin who configured the repo.
Each discovered playbook is walked one at a time by parser.parse, which creates a fresh walk with an empty specs map.
For each distinct role the playbook uses (up to 512), walk.spec reads meta/argument_specs.yml (up to 512 KiB) through w.read. Only its raw bytes count against the 16 MiB walk cap.

The parsed tree (s.root) and its yamlFile (s.y) are stored in w.sources (line 322) and w.specs (line 324) and stay reachable until the walk finishes. This also happens when readRoleSpec then reports the role as unreadable.

evidence.description: maxWalkBytes = 16 MiB limits the raw bytes read per walk, not the heap kept. 31 x 524 287-byte specs plus the playbook stay under it.
walk.read adds only len(data), the raw file bytes, to w.rawBytes. The cost of the parse tree is never charged.
w.specs[key] = s keeps the parse for the rest of the walk. No path drops s.root or s.y after the entry point is mapped.
parser.parse creates a fresh specs map for each walk, so the kept trees are freed only when that playbook's walk returns. The peak is per walk and does not add up across playbooks.

The bundled worker service sets restart: unless-stopped and no memory limit (no mem_limit, deploy.resources or GOMEMLIMIT anywhere in deploy/ or the Go code). Whether ~1.4 GB live (up to ~2.8 GB peak) ends the worker, or puts pressure on the manager and Postgres on the same host, depends on the deployment.

blockers: The full-scale walk (31 roles x 512 KiB, about 1.37 GB live, up to about 2.8 GB with GOGC=100) was not run. The approved sandbox has a 2 GiB memory cgroup that also holds the tmpfs build cache. Bounded runs up to 24 roles (1.06 GB live, linear at 84.5x) were measured; 31 roles is an extrapolation of that linear trend.

Whether the transient peak ends the worker, or affects other services, depends on the memory the deployed worker container or host has. The bundled compose sets no memory limit and runs the worker next to the manager and Postgres. The repository does not fix this, and it decides whether the effect reaches beyond the org that owns the worker.

validation_plan.local: In an offline sandbox with a memory cgroup of at least 4 GiB (otherwise the same flags as the approved sandbox), run TestVerifyRetainedHeapScale (scratch/src/internal/varsource/zz_verify_mem_test.go) with roles = 31 and the default GOGC. Record HeapAlloc at the probe role and the cgroup's memory.peak. Then repeat with a build where walk.spec keeps only the mapped entry-point results, or a node-count budget, instead of s.root/s.y (and imports drop their trees once visited). Confirm the probe-time heap stays within a small multiple of one file's parse (about 45 MB).
validation_plan.deployment: The owner reads the memory available to each deployed worker: docker stats or the cgroup memory.max of the pulsix-worker container, the host's free memory, and whether it shares the host with the manager and Postgres. Compare that with a transient peak of about 1.4 to 2.8 GB during one sync, and check the restart policy and any host OOM-killer settings. This is a read-only check, with no load test against production.

title: Existing worker clones ignore a changed repository URL and keep fetching (with the current credential) from the old origin
description: Once a worker holds a clone of a repository (<RepoCacheDir>/<org>/<repo-id>/.git), every later sync and repository-playbook run updates it with 'git fetch --quiet -- origin <branch>' and 'git reset --hard FETCH_HEAD'. The URL from the claim is used on that path only as the redaction string, and nothing on the worker reads, compares or rewrites remote.origin.url. When an org admin edits the repository URL (repos.Service.Update), or an instance admin edits a shared repository definition that propagates the URL to every projection, the manager clears the host-key pin and the next claim carries the new URL, but workers that already cloned it keep pulling from the old source. Runs execute the old source's playbooks against the organization's hosts, syncs install its requirements and report its variable sources, and the repository's current git credential is in the fetch's environment (token via GIT_ASKPASS, or ssh key via GIT_SSH_COMMAND), so git offers it to the old host if that host asks for authentication. For ssh remotes this holds while the repository is unpinned or the old and new URLs name the same ssh host (for example a repository moved to another path on the same provider): once a pin for a different new host exists (the URL change clears the pin, and only a worker that freshly clones the new URL can capture a new one), the stale worker's strict host-key check against the seeded new-host entry fails before ssh authenticates, so that worker's syncs and runs error out instead. https remotes have no pin and are not limited this way. Workers without a clone clone the new URL, so workers in the same zone can run different code for the same repository. The repo cache sweep removes clones only for repositories that no longer exist, so the stale clone stays for the life of the worker's data dir.
root_cause: Runner.fetchGit (internal/worker/runner/gitrepo.go:228-237) treats an existing clone as the authority on its source: the update path fetches the remote name 'origin', whose URL was fixed by the first 'git clone -- <spec.URL>' (gitrepo.go:249-250), instead of spec.URL. The cache key (<org>/<repo-id>) stays the same when the URL changes, and no other worker code checks or re-points the remote.
intended_behavior: Every fetch should come from the URL currently configured on the repository (the claim payload's url), and the repository's credential should only be offered to that source. A URL change, which the manager already treats as a move to a different server by clearing the host-key pin (internal/repos/service.go:367-369, shared.sql UpdateProjectedRepo), should take effect on every worker, including workers that already hold a clone.

trace.description: An org admin's repository edit sets next.URL to the new URL under the same repository id. The only side effect of a URL change is clearing the host-key pin (lines 367-369). Shared-definition edits propagate the URL to projections through UpdateAndPropagate in the same way (internal/db/queries/shared.sql:196-200).
The next run or sync claim carries the new url in the repo payload, and the repository's current credential is placed under git:<repo-id> (line 1176).
The sync passes the spec (new URL) and the git:<repo-id> credential to FetchRepoDir. The run path does the same through Runner.fetchRepo (internal/worker/runner/playbook.go:96 -> gitrepo.go:81).
A git_token credential is exposed through GIT_ASKPASS (a git_key through GIT_SSH_COMMAND at line 166) for whatever host git contacts, then fetchGit is called (line 193).
An existing <cacheRoot>/<org>/<repo-id>/.git selects the update path.
'git fetch --quiet -- origin <branch>' contacts the clone's stored origin URL, not spec.URL. 'reset --hard FETCH_HEAD' (line 234) then checks out that remote's content for the run or sync.

evidence.description: The update path fetches the remote name 'origin'. spec.URL is passed to runGit only as redactURL.
Only the fresh-clone branch passes spec.URL to git, and git records it as remote.origin.url.
URL changes are allowed and treated as a server change (the pin is cleared), but nothing invalidates or re-points worker clones.
The sweep removes an org's clone only when the repository id is no longer listed, so a URL change never removes the old clone.
A shared-definition URL edit rewrites every projection's url under the same repository id (clearing pins), so the same stale clone applies to every organization's workers.

A pinned claim seeds the run's known_hosts for the claim URL's host and fetches with StrictHostKeyChecking=yes (internal/worker/gitssh.go:77-78), so a stale ssh fetch to a different old host fails before authentication once the new URL is pinned; https fetches and same-host ssh moves are unaffected.

conditions.description: The worker already holds a clone of the repository from before the URL change (any earlier sync or run of that repository on that worker's data dir).

The repository URL has to be changed by an org admin (or by an instance admin for a shared definition). The party who benefits needs no Pulsix role: it is whoever controls, or later gains control of, the content or host at the old URL, for example an abandoned, compromised, mistyped or squatted source that the admin replaced.
Standard git semantics: 'git fetch origin' resolves the remote URL stored by 'git clone'. The verifier observed this with the git 2.47.3 shipped in noixdev/pulsix-worker:dev.

The credential-disclosure half applies only when the repository has a git_token and the old https host requests HTTP authentication, or when a git_key is used against an old ssh host while no pin for a different new ssh host is set (a pin seeds known_hosts for the new URL's host and StrictHostKeyChecking=yes then refuses the old host before authentication; a stale-clone worker never captures a new pin itself because ObservedGitHostKey looks up the new URL's host name). That half follows from the environment construction in source and was not observed against a live authenticating server.

execution.attacker_perspective: Controller of a repository source that an organization used to configure and has since replaced. The effect was observed through the worker's own git invocations in sandboxed harnesses.
payloads: Hunter harnesses (golang sandbox, fake git): FetchRepoDir(spec{URL:"https://old-host.example.invalid/team/playbooks.git",Branch:"main"}, "") followed by FetchRepoDir(spec{same org and repo id, URL:"https://new-host.example.invalid/team/playbooks.git"}, `{"token":"TOKEN-FOR-NEW-HOST"}`)

instructions: Source: confirm in internal/worker/runner/gitrepo.go:228-237 that the update path passes 'origin' rather than spec.URL to git, and that spec.URL reaches git only in the clone at line 250.

Hunter harness: in the approved golang:1.27.1-alpine sandbox, run the runner-package tests TestAuditChangedRepoURLKeepsOldOrigin and TestH10FetchExistingCloneIgnoresClaimURL (fake git that logs argv and the GIT_ASKPASS answer). remediation.strategy: On the update path, fetch from the claim's URL instead of the stored remote (or compare remote.origin.url with spec.URL and re-clone on a mismatch), so the credential, the pin check and the fetched content all go with the URL the manager currently has configured. Add a regression test where a second FetchRepoDir with a different URL hands that URL to git and never contacts the old one.

likelihood.reason: Requires a URL change on a repository that a worker already cloned, while the old source stays reachable and someone other than the organization controls it, or asks for credentials. URL changes are rare and the old source is often still the organization's own.

impact.reason: Playbooks from a source the organization removed run against its managed hosts with the org's machine credentials, and the repository's current git token or key can be offered to the old host. The UI shows the new URL, so the operator believes the change took effect.

confidence.reason: The worker control flow is fully visible in source, the argv was observed through the real fetchGit in fake-git harnesses, and the worker image's own git was observed resolving 'origin' to the old URL and checking out the old source's content. Only the credential prompt against a live authenticating old host was not exercised.

title: Run-output redaction misses a secret printed through to_yaml/to_nice_yaml (single-quoted) or urlencode
description: The worker's run-output redactor replaces only an enumerated list of literal spellings of each claim secret: the value, its JSON and nested-JSON forms, its Python repr forms (the run-3 fix) and its base64 forms. Two everyday, reversible Ansible/Jinja2 transformations with named producers are missing: the YAML single-quoted scalar that to_yaml/to_nice_yaml emit for a string that cannot be a plain scalar (for example one with a leading indicator such as @, `, !, % or containing ': '), with every ' doubled, and the percent-encoding that the urlencode filter emits (the usual way a password goes into a connection URL). A secret extra var, inventory secret or credential printed in either form by a task (debug of a rendered config, a module result holding a DSN) reaches the stored run log unchanged, and the run log is readable by every org member with jobs.read, which is the viewer role. Backlog 7.9 already lists YAML spellings as 'not done'.
root_cause: newRedactor (internal/worker/runner/redact.go:52-105) builds the redact set from a fixed list of spelling generators (plain value, reprSpellings, jsonSpellings, nestedJSONSpellings, base64Spellings, per-line pieces). redactor.text (redact.go:299-306) does a literal strings.ReplaceAll with that set. It generates no YAML single-quoted body (quote doubled) and no percent-encoded spelling, and nothing on the manager side redacts again (internal/grpcsrv/events.go:100-109 stores the payload as received).
intended_behavior: Viewers with jobs.read never see a credential, secret extra var or secret inventory var that a task printed (internal/jobs/redact.go:1-5). The redactor's own policy is to cover every reversible transformation that has a named producer (internal/worker/runner/redact.go:269-274).

trace.description: When the job is claimed, an operator-configured template's secret-typed extra var values go into the claim's redact list as plain strings. Credentials and inventory secrets are added the same way at lines 701-704. A play run by an operator then prints the value.
Expands each value into its plain, repr, JSON, nested-JSON, base64 and per-line spellings only. It adds no YAML single-quoted body and no percent-encoded body.
Passes each mapped ansible-runner event's host, task and payload (event_data.res and the display stdout) through red.eventPayload. Display-only lines go through red.textPayload at line 440.
Literal ReplaceAll over the list. '@Pa''ss!w0rd' and %40Pa%27ss%21w0rd match no entry and pass through unchanged.
The manager appends host, task, state and payload as received, with no second redaction.

title: Passkey registration finished with a session principal resolved before an admin ResetSecondFactor can add a passkey after the reset
description: An instance admin uses ResetSecondFactor (internal/accounts/actions.go) to lock someone out of an account. In one transaction, under the users row lock, it deletes every TOTP secret, recovery code and passkey, revokes every session and voids reset links. It does not delete pending webauthn_ceremonies, and it cannot affect requests already in flight. CookieMiddleware resolves the session cookie into a Principal once, when the request headers arrive (middleware.go:31), before huma reads the body. huma v2.40.0 then reads the JSON body under a default 5 s per-operation BodyReadTimeout, before it calls the handler, and http.Server sets only ReadHeaderTimeout. A client can therefore send the headers of POST /api/v1/auth/passkeys/register/finish while its session is still live and send the body later, for example once a parallel GET /auth/me returns 401. When the handler runs, requireEnrolmentSession accepts the snapshot (MFAComplete=true, MustChangePassword=false). requireFreshFactor reads Enrolled live; the reset has just removed every factor, so Enrolled is false and the freshness check is skipped. FinishRegistration takes the ceremony, which is checked only for kind and user id and survived the reset, verifies the attestation and inserts the passkey with an unconditional INSERT. completeEnrolment does nothing for an MFA-complete principal, so the request returns 200. Passkey login then gives the attacker an MFA-complete session. Without a temporary password the attacker has full access again. With one, the attacker's sessions are held at password_change_required until the owner changes the password. Preconditions for the passkey path: register/begin takes no request body (passkey_handlers.go:89, *struct{}), so it runs as soon as the headers arrive and cannot be parked. The ceremony must therefore be begun before the reset, while the account still has a factor, so the attacker must pass requireFreshFactor at begin: a factor proven within StepUpWindow (5 min), and a ceremony used within CeremonyTTL (5 min). For this path the attacker is someone who holds an account factor (or a session that proved one in the last 5 minutes), which is the person a second-factor reset is meant to lock out; a cookie alone, without a fresh factor, is not enough for the passkey path. A parked finish request that times out never reaches the handler and does not consume the ceremony, so the attacker can open a new parked request every few seconds for the life of the ceremony and renew the ceremony with a step-up. Variants with the same root cause: (a) TOTP enrol and confirm (both take a codeInput body, so both can be parked) under stale principals. This variant needs only an MFA-complete session cookie, not a fresh factor: after the reset requireFreshFactor is exempt because Enrolled is false, and TOTP.BeginEnrol asks for no code when no secret exists, so the attacker parks an enrol and a confirm request before the reset, sends the enrol body after it, computes a code from the returned secret and sends the confirm body. MarkSessionMFAComplete selects the session by id only, with no revoked_at or expires_at predicate, so ConfirmTOTP commits a confirmed secret chosen by the attacker for a revoked session. Signing in with that secret also needs the password; without the password the planted factor still blocks the owner's re-enrolment (the owner's next pending session must verify a factor the owner does not have) until an admin resets again. (b) A passkey login whose assertion was validated just before the reset creates a live MFA-complete session after it. Sessions.Create is not re-validated against the reset. The bundled compose proxy (Traefik, deploy/compose/docker-compose.yml) configures no request-buffering middleware on the manager router, so the parked-body window is not removed there.
claimed_root_cause: Credential-adding writes (Passkeys.FinishRegistration -> AddCredential/InsertPasskey, TOTP BeginEnrol/ConfirmEnrol, and Sessions.Create in FinishLogin) are authorised against a session Principal resolved before the request body is read. They are neither serialised on the users row lock that ResetSecondFactor takes (they do not re-check under it) nor conditioned on the authorising session still being live (Sessions.StillValid exists but is not used). requireFreshFactor exempts an account with no enrolled factor, and the reset produces exactly that state. Registration ceremonies are bound to the user only and survive the reset. MarkSessionMFAComplete does not filter revoked or expired sessions.

trace.description: Route for an attacker-held interactive cookie session. huma reads its JSON body (ceremony_id, name, attestation response) under a 5 s default BodyReadTimeout before the handler runs, so the body can arrive after an admin's reset has committed.
The Principal (MFAComplete, MFAAt, MustChangePassword) is resolved once via Sessions.Lookup when the headers arrive (mounted at api.go:407) and is never re-validated for this request.
Accepts the snapshot: MFAComplete=true and MustChangePassword=false admit the request without a live session check.
Enrolled is read live. After ResetSecondFactor it is false, so the function returns nil and the step-up check (passkey_handlers.go:116) is skipped because the lock-out removed every factor.

Concurrent admin action under withAccount (LockAccount FOR UPDATE): DeleteSecondFactors, RevokeAllSessions and VoidResetTokens, then commit. Pending webauthn_ceremonies and in-flight requests are untouched.

The ceremony taken by TakeCeremony (passkeys.sql:20) is checked only for kind and owning user id. There is no binding to a session or reset generation, so a ceremony begun before the reset is still accepted.

InsertPasskey commits a new passkey for the account after the reset. Its FK lock on users waits for the reset transaction if that is still open, then succeeds because the users row still exists. The handler then returns 200 (completeEnrolment is a no-op at session_gates.go:248).

evidence.description: register/begin takes *struct{} (no body), so it cannot be parked. It runs requireFreshFactor while the account still has factors, so the attacker needs a factor proven within StepUpWindow before the reset to obtain a ceremony.

LockAccount takes users FOR UPDATE. ResetSecondFactor's deletes and revocations run under it, but no enrolment write takes or re-checks under this lock, so they serialise after the reset instead of being refused.

DeleteSecondFactors deletes totp_secrets, recovery_codes and passkeys only. webauthn_ceremonies rows for the user survive (the only other deletes are TakeCeremony and the expiry reaper in passkeys.sql).
InsertPasskey is an unconditional INSERT with no predicate on a live session or a reset generation.
completeEnrolment returns without touching the session when the snapshot was MFA-complete, so no step of the request notices that the session was revoked.
MarkSessionMFAComplete's CTE selects the session by id only (no revoked_at/expires_at predicate, unlike GetSession at auth.sql:27), so it updates 1 row for a revoked session (variant a).

ConfirmTOTP relies on MarkMFAComplete returning ErrNotFound for an ended session to roll back the confirmation. Its doc comment promises 'an already-ended session returns ErrNotFound and changes nothing', but the SQL does not enforce this for a revoked session.
FinishLogin creates an MFA-complete session after validating against a credential read earlier in the request. A reset that commits in between does not prevent the session (variant b).
Sessions.StillValid already re-checks a session mid-request (used by the job log stream, backlog 7.22). The enrolment routes do not use it or any equivalent.

Only ReadHeaderTimeout is set on http.Server. Reading the body after the middleware is bounded only by huma v2.40.0's default per-operation BodyReadTimeout (5 s, huma.go:1567-1569, applied before the handler at huma.go:1041-1043).

POST /api/v1/auth/totp/enrol and /totp/confirm (line 132) take a codeInput body, so both can be parked. Enrol runs requireEnrolmentSession and requireFreshFactor (exempt once the reset removed every factor); TOTP.BeginEnrol (totp.go:154) asks for a code only when a confirmed secret exists. Variant (a) therefore needs only a pre-reset MFA-complete cookie.

The bundled Traefik router for the manager (labels at lines 115-119) declares no middleware, in particular no buffering middleware, so request bodies are streamed to the manager and the parked-body window applies behind the bundled proxy.

blockers: The end-to-end result needs the real Postgres-backed stores: a ceremony surviving DeleteSecondFactors, InsertPasskey committing after the reset, and MarkSessionMFAComplete reporting 1 row for a revoked session. internal/db/testdb and internal/api/apitest start Postgres through testcontainers and the host Docker socket, which the approved sandbox forbids (--network none, no Docker socket). The API Deps use the concrete *auth.Sessions over gen.Queries, so there is no DB-free fake path through the handlers. No reproduction was run, and no artifact supports the claim.

Whether a custom (non-bundled) reverse proxy in front of the manager buffers request bodies is a deployment fact not visible in source. The bundled compose Traefik router declares no buffering middleware, so this blocker concerns only other proxies. Buffering removes the parked-body widening of the window, but not the base race between handler entry and the reset commit.

validation_plan.local: In a disposable checkout with Docker available (dummy data only), add an integration test in internal/api using apitest + testdb. (1) Create user U with one passkey via the virtual authenticator, as internal/auth/passkey_registration_success_test.go does, and sign in to get MFA-complete session S with fresh mfa_at. (2) POST /api/v1/auth/passkeys/register/begin with S and keep ceremony C. (3) Resolve S's Principal with Sessions.Lookup and keep it. (4) Call accounts.Service.ResetSecondFactor(true, adminID, U) and let it commit. (5) Run the register/finish huma handler with a request context that carries the stale Principal (auth.WithPrincipal), for example through a test router that injects the kept Principal instead of CookieMiddleware, or with an http.Handler wrapper that blocks between CookieMiddleware and the huma handler until step 4 commits. Send a valid attestation for C. Vulnerable: status 200 and ListPasskeys(U) returns 1 row after the reset; POST /auth/passkeys/login/finish with that credential then returns a session cookie. Also assert directly: after RevokeSession(S), Sessions.MarkMFAComplete(S) returns a nil error instead of ErrNotFound, and Enrolment.ConfirmTOTP(U, S, validCode) after TOTP.BeginEnrol on the revoked S leaves totp_secrets.confirmed_at set. Fixed (regression): the finish returns 401/404 and zero passkeys exist; MarkMFAComplete on a revoked session returns ErrNotFound. Variant (a) with a non-fresh session: build a Principal for an MFA-complete session whose mfa_at is older than StepUpWindow, run ResetSecondFactor, then call the totp/enrol and totp/confirm handlers with that stale Principal. Vulnerable: both return 200 and totp_secrets.confirmed_at is set after the reset.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed, read-only, only for deployments that use a reverse proxy other than the bundled compose Traefik (whose router declares no buffering middleware in source): check whether that proxy buffers request bodies on /api/v1/auth/*. Without buffering, a client can hold the body of register/finish or totp/enrol and totp/confirm for up to huma's 5 s BodyReadTimeout after its session was resolved. No request against a deployed instance is needed or wanted.

title: Requirements source check skips plain scalars that yaml.v3 types as numbers but ansible-galaxy reads as path strings
description: The requirements step is documented to refuse any local source outside the repository's clone (spec 2026-11-06-requirements-cache-design.md, Constraints 'Local sources'; docs/upgrades.md 'local sources outside the repository are refused'). parseFile only adds a role src, a role name used as the source, a collection name or a collection source to plan.sources when yaml.v3 tags the scalar !!str, and checkSources resolves only plan.sources. Plain scalars such as 1e3, 1e+3 or 0o17 are !!float/!!int to yaml.v3 but strings to galaxy's PyYAML SafeLoader (YAML 1.1 floats need a dot; 0o is not a 1.1 octal). Reproduced end to end with dummy data: the Go check accepts 'collections: [{name: 1e3}]' (and 'name: ns.c, type: dir, source: 1e3') with 1e3 a symlink to ../other/ns/coll, while the quoted form is refused as outside the repository; ansible-galaxy 2.21.4 in the worker image then installs ns.coll from outside the clone, copying its regular files into the -p target. The worker's take-over copies regular files, so the outside content reaches the commit's requirements entry. Impact is bounded: galaxy runs as the play uid (or, without one, as the worker uid, as plays then do), and ShareRepoRead documents that every play on a worker can already read every checkout that worker has opened (backlog 2.106 trust model), so no read beyond what the repository's own plays can do was shown. The incremental effect is that a repository-content author can make a webhook-triggered sync, with no play run, pull a collection directory from elsewhere on the worker into its own owner-only cache entry, against the documented control. Narrowing of the hunter's claim: an outward file link inside an in-clone collection (0o17/plugins/key.pem) is kept as a symlink by galaxy 2.21.4, not copied, and the take-over refuses symlinks leaving the install, so that variant does not reach the entry. A plain .5e3 collection name is refused by checkCollectionName, and a bare '- 1e3' collection item is refused by the shape check.
root_cause: shape.go addRoleMapping (lines 185 and 190) and collection.go addCollections (line 44) append a src, name or source to plan.sources and plan.gitSources only when isString(node) is true, which means only for yaml.v3 !!str. checkSources (source.go line 50) iterates only plan.sources. Values that the two YAML loaders type differently are therefore never resolved or walked, although the same code checks names by text whatever the tag (scalarText, shape.go line 297) and its comment acknowledges that galaxy's loader may read .5e3 as a string where yaml.v3 reads a number.
intended_behavior: Every value ansible-galaxy may use as a local path (role src, role name used as the source, collection name, collection source) is resolved by checkSources whatever tag yaml.v3 gives it, and a value that leads outside the clone is refused before galaxy runs. Alternatively, such fields are refused unless they are YAML strings to both loaders.

trace.description: A sync_repo job, which can be webhook-triggered by a push, hands the fetched clone's requirements files to requirements.Service.Ensure. Runs use the same service. The file content comes from the repository, which is lower trust than the org admin who configured it.
Each counted file is parsed by parseFile into a plan, and line 173 passes that plan's sources to checkSources.
A role src is appended to p.sources only if isString(src); line 190 does the same for a role name used as the source. An unquoted 1e3 is !!float, so it is skipped (harness: sources=[]).

A collection name or source is appended to sources and gitSources only if isString(v). checkUntypedName (line 117) lets a dot-less name like 1e3 through, and a typed dir entry needs only a namespace.name name.
Only p.sources are resolved (links, '..', .git, absolute paths, file: URLs) and directory sources walked. The skipped value is never examined, and checkSources returns nil.

ansible-galaxy <kind> install -r <checked copy> -p <entry>/<kind> runs with cwd set to the file's directory in the clone. PyYAML reads 1e3 as the string '1e3'. from_requirement_dict treats it as a concrete artifact pointer, and _is_collection_dir follows the symlink, so galaxy installs the collection from outside the clone and copies its regular files into the temp entry. The take-over then publishes them in the requirements entry.

evidence.description: if isString(src) { p.sources = append(p.sources, src.Value) }: a src that is not !!str never becomes a source.
A role name is used as the source only when isString(nameNode).
Collection name and source are recorded as sources and gitSources only when isString(v).
checkSources resolves and walks only p.sources.
scalarText: names are checked by text whatever the tag, because galaxy's loader may read .5e3 as a string. The differential is known but applied only to role names, not to sources.
Galaxy argv: install -r <input copy> -p <entry>/<roles|collections>. cwd in.Dir is the clone directory of the file.

The take-over refuses symlinks that leave the install (errTakeOverLinkOut) but copies regular files, so content that galaxy copied from outside the clone is published. An outward file link kept as a link by galaxy is refused.

ShareRepoRead comment: opened checkouts stay group-readable for the life of the worker, and every play can read every checkout opened before it (backlog 2.106). This bounds the impact to what the repository's own plays could already read.
Constraint 'Local sources': a local-path source must resolve inside the clone under the confined-root rules, and anything else fails the step before galaxy runs.

conditions.description: The attacker can commit to a repository that an org admin configured in Pulsix (repository-content author). No Pulsix account is needed.

A collection directory (with galaxy.yml or MANIFEST.json), or a namespace directory of collections, exists outside the clone at a path the attacker can guess and that galaxy's uid can read. Examples are another repository's checkout or requirements entry on the same worker; every repository a worker serves belongs to the worker's organization.
A sync of the repository runs, either from a push webhook or from an operator. The installed content is used only when a play of that repository runs.

With PULSIX_WORKER_PLAY_UID set, galaxy reads only what the play uid can read. Without it, galaxy reads as the worker uid, as plays then do. In neither case does the read exceed what the repository's plays can already read under the documented worker trust model.

execution.attacker_perspective: Repository-content author pushing a commit to a repository that is synced by a Pulsix worker.
payloads:
requirements.yml:
collections:
  - name: 1e3
requirements.yml:
collections:
  - name: ns.c
    type: dir
    source: 1e3
ln -s ../other/ns/coll 1e3   # symlink committed in the repository root
instructions: Fixture (dummy data only): other/ns/coll/{galaxy.yml (namespace ns, name coll, version 1.0.0), README.md, plugins/marker.txt containing DUMMY_OUTSIDE_COLLECTION_MARKER}; repo/1e3 -> ../other/ns/coll; repo/req_plain_1e3.yml as the first payload, repo/req_typed_dir.yml as the second.

Go half: in the offline golang:1.27.1-alpine sandbox, run a harness test in internal/worker/requirements that builds the clone under os.OpenRoot (as the worker does), calls parseFile and then checkSources for the plain and the quoted forms.

Galaxy half: in the offline noixdev/pulsix-worker:dev image (ansible-core 2.21.4, worker-image sandbox flags, --network none, read-only root), cd repo and run 'ansible-galaxy collection install -r req_plain_1e3.yml -p /tmp/out_req_plain_1e3' with an empty ANSIBLE_CONFIG, ANSIBLE_COLLECTIONS_PATH=/tmp/none and ANSIBLE_COLLECTIONS_SCAN_SYS_PATH=false, then do the same for req_typed_dir.yml.
Check that the installed tree holds the outside marker. Artifacts: agents/v09-req-install/artifacts/evidence.txt (galaxy) and agents/v09-req-install/artifacts/evidence2.txt (Go check).
execution.observed_result: Go check (evidence2.txt): for 'name: 1e3', 'name: 1e+3', 'name: 0o17', the typed dir source 1e3, role src 1e3 and role name 1e3, the result was sources=[] (or the value was missing) and checkSources err=<nil>. The quoted '1e3' gave sources=["1e3"] and was refused with 'the source "1e3" is outside the repository'. Galaxy (evidence.txt): PyYAML 6.0.3 reads 1e3, 1e+3, .5e3 and 0o17 as str, and galaxy.py loads requirements with yaml_load. 'ansible-galaxy collection install -r req_plain_1e3.yml' installed 'ns.coll:1.0.0' to /tmp/out_req_plain_1e3/ansible_collections/ns/coll, including plugins/marker.txt with DUMMY_OUTSIDE_COLLECTION_MARKER as a regular file, not a link. The typed dir form installed ns.c with the same marker. An in-clone collection 0o17 holding an outward file link came out as a symlink, not as copied content.

remediation.strategy: Record every scalar's text, whatever its yaml.v3 tag, as a source (and git source) for role src, role name used as the source, collection name and collection source, so checkSources resolves it. Alternatively, refuse these fields with notRequirements when their tag is not !!str or !!null, which matches decodePlain's rule of refusing YAML that the two loaders read differently. Add regression cases for 1e3, 1e+3, .5e3 and 0o17 in each field, with a symlink leading outside the clone.

likelihood.reason: The payload is trivial for anyone who can commit to a synced repository and is triggered by a push webhook. A useful outside target must be an existing collection or namespace directory at a guessable path that galaxy's uid can read, and the effect shows only in the repository's own cache entry.

impact.reason: A documented control ('local sources outside the repository are refused') is bypassed, and content from outside the clone is installed into the commit's requirements entry. No read beyond the documented worker trust model was shown: the play uid (or the worker uid without one) can already read every checkout the worker opened from the repository's own plays, and the entry is worker-owned and owner-only. The incremental effect is that a sync, with no play run, pulls same-worker collection data into the entry. That is a defense-in-depth gap, not demonstrated disclosure or code execution.

confidence.reason: Both halves were reproduced independently in the approved offline sandboxes: the Go check over an os.Root clone accepts the plain forms and refuses the quoted ones, and ansible-core 2.21.4 in the worker image installs the outside collection's files from the plain form. The source line numbers were verified at 52f27625. The low impact rests on source-documented trust-model statements (share.go ShareRepoRead, backlog 2.106) and the org-scoped worker.
